[b]General:[/b]
Crystal Caves is a puzzle platformer game about Mylo Steamwitz trying out various getting-rich schemes for which he needs crystals. The game is split between 3 episodes, each having 16 levels to finish. In order to finish the level you need to collect all the crystals first.

Gameplay consists of various enemies you can blast off with your rocket pistol and some traps and puzzles. Even though the goal of the game is quite simple you may find the game quite difficult for you can run out of ammo, destroy wrong glass block which you needed to jump on, shoot at the air pump, let monsters overrun you... yes, the caves are a dangerous place!

Gameplay doesn't change much through the episodes where the 1st episode shows more or less everything the game has to offer. However, later episodes will surely give you a better challenge than the first ones so they are worthy of a play-through.

With that being said, the game is well played even today if you can look past the PC Speaker sounds,  EGA color graphics and other DOS era details.

[b]Replay value:[/b]
In every level you will find pickups that awards you extra points as well as eggs which you can shoot to collect B-O-N-U-S word that brings you additional 10k points. Replay value lies in beating the highscores but in case of Crystal Caves, the highscores are only saved locally so you may be only beating your own score. 

[h1]Conclusion: Crystal Caves is a great DOS game title offering just enough challenges and plenty of fun. If you feel like playing something good from the old times then Crystal Caves is for you![/h1]

A very simple linear game. Played a lot the shareware version during my chilhood, Crystal Caves is one of the Apogee's titles that spawned during the boom of platforming games on PC.

Platforming wasn't an easy task for 1991's DOS games, but this, with other titles from Apogee and another series made by Id Software itself (Commander Keen), was a fun one. 

The objective is simple: you're a miner, you have 16 levels per episode (registered version has 3 episodes, all included in this release) for collecting all the crystals in order to go on. Of course you will shoot enemies and avoid traps and various hazards, like spikes, poisoned mushrooms, etc. 

Every level is mazed-like and filled with obstacles. Sometimes the controls are a little sloppy, but you'll get used to it very quickly if you're comfortable with keyboards. In 1991 on PC it was a good game, but today it's too simple and without depth.

Some games need context. And in 1991, this one was a nice ride. Buy it only if you played this when you were a kid, or if you're curious. Just don't expect too much.

Oh my gosh! :O I can't believe this game is on steam, this is such an old game that I used to play as a kid, but I enjoyed playing it so much, it's an absolute classic, those were the good old days when good games were actually being made. One of my dad's friends (he was like an uncle) gave my sister and I a floppy disk with Crystal Caves on it. It just had the first volume on it (there's 3 volumes on this game, if you buy it on steam), but we were hooked! Now, as an adult, I still love it, such a classic game! :)
Here's the story plot - You play the role of Mylo, who is trying to come up with ways to get rich. So he flies off to a mining planet in his malfunctioning ship, the Kiwi, to look for crystals deep underground. This game has 3 volumes, when you finish the 1st volume, Mylo's idea to become rich fails, so he comes up with another idea, and tries again, in the next volume, volume 2, flying back to the mining planet to look for more crystals (cause, if you want to get rich, you have to spend money to make money, right? :D). The second volume basically ends with the same result, with Mylo's second idea to get rich failing, and he tries again in the 3rd volume. I won't give anything away, except to say that the ending of the 3rd volume has a different result :)
Each volume in this game has a bunch of levels you can do. The first volume is a blast, just so much fun to do! The best thing about this first volume is that it's not too hard to be frustrating, and not too easy to be boring, it's just in the middle, perfect! :) The second volume, though, gets harder, and I won't be doing that one again. And the majority of the levels in the 3rd volume are ridiculously hard, so I won't be doing that one again, either. I just did all 3 volumes to see what happens at the end of the story, and it was cool to see the ending, but I'll keep doing the 1st volume from now on, that one is great! :D If you like doing games with hard difficulty, then go for the 2nd and 3rd volumes, but if you like games with easier difficulty, the 1st volume is for you! There's a bunch of levels in the 1st volume to keep you entertained! :) My only complaint is that I wish the 2nd and 3rd volumes could have been easier, just like the 1st volume, but still, I absolutely love this game, definitely recommended! :)

Crystal Caves is a simple, old-fashioned 2D puzzle platformer, bearing some similarity to the very first Duke Nukem.
Each level, you need to figure out what order to do things in so that you can take out the baddies, grab all the goodies, and make it to the exit alive; it's easy to die or sometimes to get trapped so you have to quit and re-enter the level, but if you're fast and clever enough you may be able to succeed without taking a single hit for a massive score bonus. You can take as many tries as you need to beat each level (no lives limit), which makes the challenging puzzles much more forgiving, and if you get frustrated, you can go back to the main map and platform to a different level for a change of pace.
The story is silly and the action simplistic, but with Steam automatically setting up and configuring a dosbox for it, this is an easy way to relive the old days.
From a modern perspective? It's not all that exciting, but if you like retro simplicity, or are craving nostalgia, it's not bad either.

They don't make them like this anymore. After playing through it and checking out similar modern games, it's pretty obvious why.

1. The game's replayability is based off of a high score system, but simply staying in a leel and picking up  the randomly appearing fruits will allow you to get a higher score than anyone else. 
2. Obvious things that it looks like you should be able to do (such as jumping into a gap big enough for the main character) can't always be done, with some trial and erro (or memory of the old game) required to remind you of which.
3. It is entirely possible to lock yourself out of being able to complete levels (or even access them in the third game) without realising it.

If you remember the game from your childhood, and want to relive the nostalgia, then this is probably one of the better ways to do it. But the game has not aged very well, in comparison to similar games from the era, let alone from the modern climate, and so, I honestly can't recommend it.
